newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 25.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
- Local U.S. telephone companies want Internet service providers to share access costs.
- "Love Simulation" games have become the most popular home video in the industry in Japan.

- Children's books publisher Orchard Books of Grolier Inc, which in turn is owned by Lagardere Group, has sued three former editors alleging they plotted to take its authors and illustrators with them.
- At least 10 publications are trying to become the definitive guide for the Internet.
- Rhythm-and-blues group TLC has reached a contractual agreement with LaFace Records and Pebbitone Inc after having filed for bankruptcy.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin agreed to exchange state visits during the next two years.
- Health maintenance organizations are changing the way they pay physicians.
- The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has recommended stricter national standards for emissions of chemicals and particles that cause smog.
